## Context verified on the planning ref
- The script has 145 lines and starts with `set -euo pipefail` (line 13). It has **no existing `trap`**. The guards are in the order the issue describes. The fetch loop is at lines 87–102, with `fetch_attempt`, `fetch_max_attempts=4` and backoff starting at 2 s. The branch switch is at lines 104–124, the head-moved guard at 126–133, and the env writes at 135–145.
- In `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (lines 2965–2975) the step **`source`s** the script, and the `source` line is the last command in its `run:` block. An EXIT trap installed by the script therefore fires once, when the step shell exits. That covers explicit `exit`, `set -e` aborts and normal completion.
- Identifiers: only `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_REPOSITORY` exists with this prefix (a step env input, which must not be touched). Nothing named `review_head_checkout_*` exists. `REVIEW_CHECKOUT_SHA` is read only and is not reused.
- Pattern to reuse: the `ORCH_POLL_CYCLE_SUMMARY` EXIT trap in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (lines 30–146): an epoch-ms helper with a seconds×1000 fallback, a trap that receives `"$?"`, never calls `exit` and runs in `|| true` context, and an emit-once guard.
- Test harness to reuse: `test_review_branch_fetch_movement_skips_the_older_source_tree` in `tests/test_review_autofix_merge_precheck.py` (lines 120–171). It builds a real seed, source and split git layout and runs `review_autofix_step_script_body(...)` through `bash -c`.
- `tests/inventory_parity.py` only checks paths under `scripts/` (plus three audit-gate assets). The script is already listed in `docs/INVENTORY.md` (line 294), so **neither file needs an edit**. `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` only needs an edit if the new test is not wired; it will be wired in `ci.yml`, so that file is **unchanged** too. All four were in the advisory list; they are left untouched on purpose.
- `ci.yml` is 189,224 bytes, far below the 480,000-byte guard.

## Functions or modules to implement

All code goes in `scripts/review_autofix_step_checkout_pr_head_branch.sh` (tabs or the file's existing 2-space style, matching the surrounding code; no reflow of existing lines).

1. **Right after `set -euo pipefail`**, initialise state unconditionally, so nothing is inherited from the environment:
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_STAGE="pr_metadata"`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=0`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_GIT_EXIT_CLASS="none"`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_HEAD_MATCH="na"`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_START_MS=""`, `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_END_MS=""`, `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_SWITCH_START_MS=""`, `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_SWITCH_END_MS=""`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_STDERR_FILE=""`
   - `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_EMITTED=false`

   Then define three functions, set `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_START_MS` and install `trap 'review_head_checkout_on_exit "$?" || true' EXIT`. All of this goes before line 15, so a `jq` failure is also recorded.
   - `review_head_checkout_now_ms`: a copy of the `_orch_poll_cycle_now_ms` shape. It tries `date +%s%3N` and accepts it only if the result matches `^[0-9]+$`, which rejects BSD's literal `%3N`. Otherwise it returns `date +%s`×1000. It always returns 0.
   - `review_head_checkout_classify_fetch_stderr <file>`: prints one token. It uses `grep -Eiq` with fixed patterns only, checked in this order:
     - `transport_5xx`: `(HTTP|error:|status)[ :]*5[0-9]{2}`, `Internal Server Error`, `Bad Gateway`, `Service Unavailable` or `Gateway Time-?out`
     - `auth`: `Authentication failed`, `could not read (Username|Password)`, `terminal prompts disabled`, `Permission denied` or `(HTTP|error:)[ :]*40[13]`
     - `not_found`: `couldn't find remote ref`, `Repository not found`, `does not appear to be a git repository` or `(HTTP|error:)[ :]*404`
     - `network`: `Could not resolve host`, `Connection (reset|refused|timed out)`, `Operation timed out`, `Failed to connect`, `early EOF`, `unexpected disconnect`, `RPC failed`, `Recv failure`, `Empty reply`, `SSL` or `TLS`
     - otherwise `other`. A missing or unreadable file also gives `other`.
   - `review_head_checkout_on_exit <rc>`:
     - It returns at once if `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_EMITTED=true` or if `${BASHPID:-$$} != $$`. Then it sets the emitted flag.
     - It computes `duration_ms = now - START_MS`, or `0` if either value is not an integer.
     - `fetch_ms` is `END - START` when both are set, `now - START` when only the start is set (fetch was aborted), and `na` when fetch never started. `switch_ms` is computed the same way.
     - It derives `outcome`: `rc != 0` gives `failed`. Otherwise the stage decides: `head_match_guard` or `head_moved_guard` gives `skipped_stale`, `head_ref_invalid` or `head_repo_foreign` gives `skipped_no_push`, and any other stage gives `ok`.
     - It sanitises every field: integers must match `^[0-9]+$`, and tokens must be from their enum or fall back to `other`/`na`.
     - It runs `rm -f` on `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_STDERR_FILE`. This only removes the mktemp file this run created.
     - It prints exactly `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT stage=<s> outcome=<o> duration_ms=<n> fetch_ms=<n|na> switch_ms=<n|na> fetch_attempts=<n> git_exit_class=<c> head_match=<true|false|na> exit_code=<rc>` to stdout, with `2>/dev/null || true`.
     - It never calls `exit`, so bash keeps the original status. Every statement runs with `|| true`.

2. **Stage assignments.** Each is one added line placed right before the existing code; existing lines are not changed:

   | Stage | Placed before | rc 0 means | rc ≠ 0 means |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `pr_metadata` | the initial value; covers lines 15–21 | n/a | jq or env write failed |
   | `head_match_guard` | line 26 | skipped_stale | failed |
   | `workspace_guard` | line 40 | n/a | failed |
   | `opencode_guard` | line 44 | n/a | failed |
   | `head_ref_invalid` | line 51; covers both the empty and the invalid checks | skipped_no_push | failed (empty ref) |
   | `head_repo_foreign` | line 67 | skipped_no_push | n/a |
   | `ref_health_repair` | line 73; also covers `CURRENT_BRANCH` | n/a | failed |
   | `fetch` | line 87; also sets `FETCH_START_MS` | n/a | failed |
   | `branch_switch` | line 104; also sets `SWITCH_START_MS`. Set `SWITCH_END_MS` after `fi` at line 124 | n/a | failed |
   | `head_moved_guard` | line 126 | skipped_stale | failed |
   | `publish_env` | line 135 | n/a | failed |
   | `done` | after line 145 | ok | n/a |

   `pr_metadata` and `publish_env` are additions to the issue's "such as" list; see D5.

   Head-match bookkeeping:
   - Inside the line 34 `if` block, before its `exit 0`, set `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_HEAD_MATCH=false`.
   - After the line 30–37 `if/fi`, still inside the `PR_NUMBER` branch, set it to `true`.
   - Inside the line 128 block, set it to `false`. After it, still inside the `PR_NUMBER` branch, set it to `true`.
   - With a non-numeric `PR_NUMBER` it stays `na`.

3. **Fetch loop** (lines 87–102). The retry count, backoff, messages and `exit 1` stay unchanged.
   - Before the loop, run `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_STDERR_FILE="$(mktemp "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/review-head-checkout-fetch.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null || true)"`. This fails open: an empty value means the old command path.
   - At the top of each iteration, set `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_ATTEMPTS="${fetch_attempt}"`.
   - Replace the single `if git fetch …; then` with an if/else on whether the temp file exists:
     - **With a file:** `if { git fetch <same args> 2>&1 1>&3 3>&- | { tee "${REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_FETCH_STDERR_FILE}" >&2 3>&- || true; }; } 3>&1; then`. Git's stdout keeps going to stdout and its stderr is still streamed to the step's stderr. `pipefail` makes the condition reflect git's exit status, and `tee … || true` stops a temp-file write error from turning into a spurious retry. `tee` truncates the file on each attempt, so it holds only the latest attempt.
     - **Without a file:** the original command, verbatim.
   - On success, set `FETCH_END_MS` before `break`.
   - On failure, set `REVIEW_HEAD_CHECKOUT_GIT_EXIT_CLASS="$(review_head_checkout_classify_fetch_stderr "${file}" || true)"`, or `other` when there is no file, before the existing exhaustion check. When a later attempt succeeds, the line therefore still shows the class of the last *failed* attempt. With no failed attempt it stays `none`.
   - Stderr text never enters the summary line; only the enum token does.
